newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian union leader warns of social conflict.
newsitem.headline: Italian union leader warns of social conflict.

text.p: A leading Italian trade union leader warned on Saturday of "inevitable social conflict" if employers did not soften their position in a bitter pay dispute with engineering and metalworkers.

Sergio D'Antoni, leader of the CISL, one of Italy's three main trade union confederations, said fresh talks with unions and the Federmeccanica employers' federation due to start next week would be "decisive".
"If their (the employers') position does not change, then I think we will have to try and give a strong reaction," D'Antoni told a news conference.
"How we go about that remains to be seen, but certainly a new phase of inevitable social conflict would be opened."

The workers' last two-year contracts expired last June and the government, in a bid to break the impasse, has suggested that workers should be given a 200,000 lire ($130) a month pay rise for the 1996-1998 contract period.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said the offer was fair and would not fuel inflation, but the Federmeccanica has rejected the proposal and offered to raise pay by no more than 139,000 lire a month.
"If this behaviour continues, then a clear intention will have emerged, to change the rules of the game unilaterally," D'Antoni said.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu is currently in informal contact with unions and employers ahead of formal talks which he hopes to resume with both sides next week.
Unions have already held several hours of strikes within the engineering and metalworking sector throughout the country in support of their demands.
One Union leader said on Friday he saw no chance of an accord with employers in the bitter six-months dispute and pressed for a general strike to support demands.
